subject: Acceptance Passport & Meridian pilot evaluation checkpoints
messages:
From: Jill Park <jill.park@meridianhealth.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance passport and MAP for Meridian pilot

Avery — thanks again for the demo last week. Meridian is excited to run a 6-week pilot, but our internal stakeholders need a concise artifact that defines what 'pass' looks like.

High-level asks from our side: 
- A single-page "Acceptance Passport" that lists pass/fail acceptance tests (functionality, latency P95, accuracy on our de-identified test set, failure modes, and safe-output checks).
- Clear owner per gate (Redwood contact, Meridian contact).
- Exit gates for the pilot (what would cause us to stop or extend).
- A short verification runbook so our SREs can validate requests against the SLA sampling.

I've attached our security QA matrix (Meridian_Security_QA.xlsx) — it contains the audit and logging items you'll need to link to. Procurement will also want cost buckets tied to the acceptance gates (i.e., if we retain the dedicated lane).

Proposed timeline from Meridian: pilot kickoff w/c 2026-06-22, 3-week smoke then 3-week evaluation window, decision by 2026-07-27. Can Redwood produce the Acceptance Passport + sample tests by next Friday?

Thanks — Jill

Jill Park
Director, Data Platforms
Meridian Health
jill.park@meridianhealth.com
(415) 555-1987

Attachment: Meridian_Security_QA.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)
From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
To: Jill Park <jill.park@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance passport and MAP for Meridian pilot

Hi Jill — really appreciate the clarity. We're aligned on the deliverables and can produce an 'Acceptance Passport' artifact that maps pass/fail tests to specific verification steps. Draft plan below (we'll put the formal doc in Drive):

Acceptance Passport (deliverable components)
- Executive summary: one-sentence success definition tied to Meridian outcomes (safety + 95th P95 latency target).
- Exit gates: list of hard failures (e.g., P95 > 800ms for 3 consecutive days, >1% unsafe outputs on sampled set, inability to surface audit logs).
- Acceptance tests: functional smoke (end-to-end prompt/control cases), performance sampling (monthly P95/P99), accuracy / concordance tests vs. your de-id dataset, security checklist (KMS, logs, retention).
- Owners & SLA: Redwood owners (Avery — integration; Ben — rollout & failover), Meridian owners (your SRE + Data Platform).
- Rollback & fallback: model-variant fallback plan and temporary throttling thresholds.

Timeline (draft)
- 2026-06-12: Redwood to share template + draft passport (this Friday).
- 2026-06-22: Pilot kickoff (integration & baseline runs).
- 2026-07-13: End of smoke; verification run.
- 2026-07-27: Decision & proposal for next steps.

Next steps we request from Meridian by Friday: the de-identified acceptance test set (sample), procurement point-of-contact, and confirmation on the latency target (we proposed P95 <= 800ms, adjustable).

I'm attaching our template for the Acceptance Passport (redwood-acceptance-passport-template.docx) so you can see the shape. We'll populate the Meridian-specific draft and share a link.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0092

Attachment: redwood-acceptance-passport-template.docx (docx, 8 pages)

Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance passport and MAP for Meridian pilot

+1 on the Passport idea. Couple of practical points from the Dedicated/ops side: 
- We'll include an SLA sampling plan: daily P95/P99 snapshot plus a weekly 1,000-query concordance sample against Meridian's de-id test set.
- Pricing buckets should have an acceptance-boundary clause: e.g., if pilot extends due to failing exit gates, we revert to pilot rate + bps for extended weeks (helps procurement avoid surprise costs).
- For fallback: recommend a pre-approved model variant (smaller quantized model) and a regional fallback (us-west -> us-east) that we can flip if latency SLOs break.

Avery — I'll draft the SLA sampling appendix and the fallback playbook and attach to the Passport. Jill — can you please confirm who in procurement should be included? If you share their email we can include cost-appendix placeholders.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance passport and MAP for Meridian pilot

Thanks, Avery & Ben — this looks good. Procurement contact is attached (meridian-procurement-contact.vcf) and you can loop in Priya Rao (priya@meridianhealth.com).

We can confirm the latency target at P95 <= 800ms for the pilot window. Our SREs will prepare the de-identified sample set and upload to the Drive folder you linked.

Two quick clarifications: 
- For the exit gates, can we make the >1% unsafe-output threshold a rolling 48-hour window rather than an instantaneous spike? That will reduce noisy false positives.
- For the fallback model, we want the region-aware switch to be manual for the pilot (operations-run) — automatic region fallback is OK to document, but please keep the manual execution for safety & auditability.

If you can push the draft Passport by EOD Monday we'll review it and add our SRE/Procurement annotations. Appreciate the responsiveness.

— Jill
